title: I was convinced Google Drive was just storage until Gemini changed everything
excerpt: These Gemini features deserve the spotlight
content_html:
Published Aug 11, 2026, 11:15 AM EDT

I cover Android with a focus on productivity, automation, and Google’s ecosystem, including Gemini and everyday apps. With a background in engineering and software development, I tend to go beyond surface-level tips and focus on how features fit into real workflows.
Before joining AP, I wrote for tech publications such as Gizbot in 2023 and iJunkie (formerly known as iPhoneHacks) from 2021 to 2022.

I've always used Google Drive to store files, but for years, that's all I thought it was. I'd upload something, file it away, and search for it when I needed it.

That changed when I discovered how much more Drive can do. I can now search using natural language, ask questions about files, summarize folders, compare documents, and use Gemini to help organize everything I've accumulated.

These are the Google Drive features I think deserve more attention.

I stopped searching for file names

I started describing what I wanted instead

I used to think I had to remember a file's name to find it in Google Drive. That became a problem when I knew what I was looking for but had no idea what I'd called it.

Now, I can describe what I remember.

With Gemini in Drive, I can use natural-language prompts to search for files based on their contents or context rather than an exact filename.

For example, instead of searching for a vague document name, I can ask Drive to find a presentation about a particular project or a PDF someone shared with me recently.

That feels much closer to how I remember things. I rarely remember that a file was called Project_Final_v2.pdf. I remember that it contained a budget, was shared with me last month, and had something to do with a particular project.

Many of the newer Gemini features discussed here require a Google AI subscription or an eligible Google Workspace plan.

I can turn a document into something I can listen to

Gemini turns my documents into audio

Some documents can be tedious to read, especially when they run for dozens of pages.

Google Drive's Gemini-powered audio overview gives me another option. I can turn a supported document into an AI-generated audio summary and listen to it instead of reading the whole file at once.

To try it, find the document in Google Drive on the web, click the three-dot menu icon beside it, and select Create an audio overview.

Gemini creates an audio discussion that highlights the key points from the document, which I can listen to while commuting, walking, or doing something else.

Audio overviews in Google Drive work with PDFs, Google Docs, Google Slides, Microsoft Word and PowerPoint files, plain-text files, and videos. The feature is currently available in English.

It's a convenient way to get familiar with a long document before deciding whether I need to read it from beginning to end.

I can ask what's inside a folder before opening everything

Gemini gives me the gist of a folder first

I've accumulated plenty of folders in Google Drive that I rarely revisit because I don't remember exactly what's inside them. Instead of opening files one by one, I can now ask Gemini for an overview of a folder.

Open Google Drive on the web, find the folder you want to explore, click the three-dot menu icon beside it, and select Ask Gemini.

Gemini can summarize the folder's contents and give you an overview of the files, so you can get the gist without opening them individually. You can then ask follow-up questions about the folder or specific files.

It saves me from the familiar routine of opening several documents to figure out which one contains the information I need.

I can compare information instead of opening files side by side

I stopped flipping between documents to find differences

I used to compare documents the slow way: open one file, open another, switch between tabs, and try to remember what changed. Gemini in Google Drive gives me a faster option when I'm working with multiple related files.

I can select relevant files as sources and ask Gemini to compare the information across them.

For example, I could ask it to compare two versions of a document, highlight differences between reports, or pull out conflicting details from several files.

Gemini can use multiple files as sources and synthesize the information into a single response.

To use it, I click Ask Gemini (sparkle icon) in Drive and type @file name to add the files I want it to use as sources. Then, I can ask a specific comparison question. I can also ask follow-up questions if I want Gemini to dig deeper.

I can turn my files into a Project

I stopped rebuilding the same context

If I'm working on something that involves the same group of documents, I can save them as a Project instead of repeatedly adding the same sources.

I can then return to the Project and continue asking Gemini questions using that same collection of files as its foundation.

To create one, open Google Drive on the web, click New > New Project, give it a name, and add the files, folders, or emails you want to use as sources.

I can also save an existing Gemini conversation as a Project.

It's especially beneficial for ongoing projects, allowing me to revisit them later without needing to establish the same context.

I can also share Projects with others while leaving the original files in their existing Drive locations.

Google Drive is more than a place to store files

I used to think of Google Drive as a place to dump files and forget about them until I needed them again. Now, I have found more reasons to use it.

From smarter search and folder summaries to Gemini's ability to compare files and turn documents into audio, Drive has become much more useful than I realized.

It turns a storage service into an assistant that can help me make sense of what I have already collected.

content_html_zh:
发布于 2026 年 8 月 11 日，美国东部时间上午 11:15

我介绍 Android 时，重点关注生产力、自动化和 Google 生态系统，包括 Gemini 和日常应用程序。 凭借工程和软件开发的背景，我倾向于超越表面技巧，而专注于功能如何融入实际工作流程。 在加入 AP 之前，我曾为科技出版物撰写文章，例如 2023 年为 Gizbot 撰写文章，2021 年至 2022 年为 iJunkie（以前称为 iPhoneHacks）撰写文章。

我一直使用 Google 云端硬盘来存储文件，但多年来，我一直以为它就是这样。 我会上传一些东西，将其归档，然后在需要时进行搜索。

当我发现 Drive 可以做更多事情时，情况发生了变化。 我现在可以使用自然语言进行搜索、提出有关文件的问题、总结文件夹、比较文档，并使用 Gemini 帮助组织我积累的所有内容。

我认为这些是 Google Drive 的功能值得更多关注。

我停止搜索文件名

我开始描述我想要的东西

我曾经认为我必须记住文件名才能在 Google 云端硬盘中找到它。 当我知道我在寻找什么但不知道我该如何称呼它时，这就成了一个问题。

现在，我可以描述我所记得的事情了。

借助云端硬盘中的 Gemini，我可以使用自然语言提示根据文件的内容或上下文而不是确切的文件名来搜索文件。

例如，我可以要求云端硬盘查找有关特定项目的演示文稿或某人最近与我共享的 PDF，而不是搜索模糊的文档名称。

这感觉更接近我记忆中的事情。 我很少记得有一个文件名为 Project_Final_v2.pdf。 我记得它包含一份预算，上个月与我分享，并且与特定项目有关。

此处讨论的许多 Gemini 新功能都需要订阅 Google AI 或符合条件的 Google Workspace 套餐。

我可以将文档变成我可以听的东西

Gemini 将我的文档变成音频

有些文档读起来可能很乏味，尤其是当它们长达数十页时。

Google Drive 的 Gemini 音频概述为我提供了另一种选择。 我可以将受支持的文档转换为人工智能生成的音频摘要并收听它，而不是立即阅读整个文件。

要尝试一下，请在网络版 Google 云端硬盘中找到该文档，单击其旁边的三点菜单图标，然后选择“创建音频概述”。

Gemini 创建了一个音频讨论，突出显示了文档中的要点，我可以在上下班、散步或做其他事情时收听。

Google 云端硬盘中的音频概述适用于 PDF、Google 文档、Google 幻灯片、Microsoft Word 和 PowerPoint 文件、纯文本文件和视频。 该功能目前提供英文版本。

在决定是否需要从头到尾阅读之前，这是一种熟悉长文档的便捷方法。

在打开所有内容之前我可以询问文件夹内有什么

Gemini 首先告诉我文件夹的要点

我在 Google 云端硬盘中积累了很多文件夹，但我很少重新访问它们，因为我不记得它们里面到底有什么。 我现在可以向 Gemini 询问文件夹的概述，而不是逐个打开文件。

在网络上打开 Google 云端硬盘，找到您要浏览的文件夹，单击其旁边的三点菜单图标，然后选择询问 Gemini。

Gemini 可以总结文件夹的内容并为您提供文件的概述，因此您无需单独打开它们即可了解要点。 然后，您可以询问有关文件夹或特定文件的后续问题。

它使我不必再像熟悉的那样打开多个文档来找出哪一个包含我需要的信息。

我可以比较信息而不是并排打开文件

我不再翻阅文档来寻找差异

我过去常常以缓慢的方式比较文档：打开一个文件，打开另一个文件，在选项卡之间切换，并尝试记住发生了什么变化。 当我处理多个相关文件时，Google 云端硬盘中的 Gemini 为我提供了更快的选择。

我可以选择相关文件作为来源，并要求 Gemini 比较它们之间的信息。

例如，我可以要求它比较文档的两个版本，突出显示报告之间的差异，或者从多个文件中提取冲突的详细信息。

Gemini 可以使用多个文件作为源，并将信息合成为单个响应。

要使用它，我在云端硬盘中单击“询问 Gemini”（闪烁图标），然后输入@文件名以添加我希望其用作源的文件。 然后，我可以提出一个具体的比较问题。 如果我想让双子座更深入地挖掘，我也可以提出后续问题。

我可以将我的文件变成一个项目

我停止重建相同的上下文

如果我正在处理涉及同一组文档的内容，我可以将它们另存为项目，而不是重复添加相同的源。

然后我可以返回该项目并使用相同的文件集合作为其基础继续询问 Gemini 问题。

要创建一个，请在网络上打开 Google 云端硬盘，单击“新建”>“新建项目”，为其命名，然后添加要用作源的文件、文件夹或电子邮件。

我还可以将现有的 Gemini 对话保存为项目。

这对于正在进行的项目特别有益，使我可以稍后重新访问它们，而无需建立相同的上下文。

我还可以与其他人共享项目，同时将原始文件保留在现有的云端硬盘位置。

Google 云端硬盘不仅仅是一个存储文件的地方

我曾经认为 Google Drive 是一个转储文件并忘记它们的地方，直到我再次需要它们。 现在，我找到了更多使用它的理由。

从更智能的搜索和文件夹摘要到 Gemini 比较文件和将文档转换为音频的能力，Drive 变得比我想象的更有用。

它将存储服务变成了助手，可以帮助我理解我已经收集的内容。
